name: NIST CSF 2.0
description: NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 — 6 functions (GOVERN, IDENTIFY, PROTECT, DETECT, RESPOND, RECOVER), 22 categories, 106 subcategories. This is a reporting layer cross-referencing NIST SP 800-53 MODERATE baseline results. Each CSF category maps to one or more 800-53 controls. Verification comes from parent benchmarks via the 800-53 aggregation.
honest_disclosure: CSF is a framework for organizing results, not a checklist. This file shows how our existing 800-53 findings map to CSF functions and categories. Scores are derived from the NIST 800-53 report, which derives from DISA/CIS/PCI-DSS/OWASP parent benchmarks.

group_policies.name: GOVERN (GV) — Organizational Context
group_policies.description: The organization's cybersecurity risk management strategy, expectations, and policy are established, communicated, and monitored. This function is NEW in CSF 2.0.

items.title: Policy (GV.PO)
items.description: Organizational cybersecurity policies for managing risk are established, communicated, and enforced.
items.regulation: NIST CSF 2.0 GV.PO → SP 800-53 PM-1, PL-4
items.remediation: Document and publish cybersecurity policies. Review annually.

items.title: Risk Management Strategy (GV.RM)
items.description: Cybersecurity risks are identified, assessed, prioritized, and managed as part of the organization's enterprise risk management strategy.
items.regulation: NIST CSF 2.0 GV.RM → SP 800-53 RA-5, PM-9
items.remediation: Implement risk management framework. Conduct annual risk assessments. Track findings to remediation.

items.title: Supply Chain Risk Management (GV.SC)
items.description: Cybersecurity supply chain risk management processes are identified, established, and managed.
items.regulation: NIST CSF 2.0 GV.SC → SP 800-53 SR-2, SR-3
items.remediation: Assess third-party service providers. Include security requirements in vendor contracts.

group_policies.name: IDENTIFY (ID) — Asset & Risk Awareness
group_policies.description: Develop organizational understanding to manage cybersecurity risk to systems, assets, data, and capabilities

items.title: Asset Management (ID.AM)
items.description: Data, personnel, devices, systems, and facilities that enable the organization to achieve business purposes are identified and managed.
items.remediation: Maintain asset inventory. Publish security.txt. Document all web assets and dependencies.

items.title: Risk Assessment (ID.RA)
items.description: The organization understands the cybersecurity risk to operations, assets, and individuals.
items.remediation: Conduct regular vulnerability assessments. Track threat intelligence relevant to web applications.

group_policies.name: PROTECT (PR) — Safeguards
group_policies.description: Develop and implement safeguards to ensure delivery of critical services. The largest function — covers access control, awareness, data security, protective technology.

items.title: Identity Management, Authentication and Access Control (PR.AC)
items.description: Access to physical and logical assets is limited to authorized users, processes, and devices, and is managed consistent with the assessed risk.
items.regulation: NIST CSF 2.0 PR.AC → SP 800-53 AC-2, AC-3, AC-7, AC-11, AC-14, IA-5
items.remediation: Implement account management, access enforcement, session management, and strong authentication policies.

items.title: Data Security (PR.DS)
items.description: Information and records are managed consistent with the organization's risk strategy to protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information.
items.regulation: NIST CSF 2.0 PR.DS → SP 800-53 SC-8, SC-13, SC-23
items.remediation: Encrypt all data in transit with TLS 1.2+. Use Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite cookies. Enable HSTS.

items.title: Protective Technology (PR.PT)
items.description: Technical security solutions are managed to ensure the security and resilience of systems and assets.
items.regulation: NIST CSF 2.0 PR.PT → SP 800-53 CM-7, SC-7, SI-10, SI-11, AC-23
items.remediation: Harden web server configuration. Deploy CSP, WAF, and custom error pages. Block data mining crawlers.

items.title: Information Protection Processes and Procedures (PR.IP)
items.description: Security policies, processes, and procedures are maintained and used to manage protection of information systems.
items.remediation: Document secure configuration baselines. Implement change management for all web server configuration changes.

group_policies.name: DETECT (DE) — Continuous Monitoring
group_policies.description: Develop and implement activities to identify the occurrence of a cybersecurity event

items.title: Continuous Monitoring (DE.CM)
items.description: The information system and assets are monitored to identify cybersecurity events and verify the effectiveness of protective measures.
items.regulation: NIST CSF 2.0 DE.CM → SP 800-53 SI-2, AU-2
items.remediation: Enable web server logging. Monitor for CVEs. Implement file integrity monitoring (FIM).

group_policies.name: RESPOND (RS) — Incident Response
group_policies.description: Take action regarding a detected cybersecurity incident

items.title: Response Planning (RS.RP)
items.description: Response processes and procedures are executed and maintained to ensure timely response to detected cybersecurity incidents.
items.regulation: NIST CSF 2.0 RS.RP → SP 800-53 IR-4, IR-8
items.remediation: Create and maintain an incident response plan. Define roles, communication procedures, and escalation paths. Test annually.

group_policies.name: RECOVER (RC) — Resilience
group_policies.description: Maintain resilience plans and restore capabilities or services impaired by an incident

items.title: Recovery Planning (RC.RP)
items.description: Recovery processes and procedures are executed and maintained to ensure timely restoration of systems or assets affected by cybersecurity incidents.
items.remediation: Implement automated backups with offsite storage. Test restoration procedures quarterly.
